A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study with complete, readable main text and Appendix A. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that the scientific content, figures, and tables match.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of annotation reliability, LLM–expert review agreement, and rejection decisions in Tables 2–5, with further results and annotation analyses in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original annotation-reliability, review-agreement, and rejection-decision results in Tables 2–5 and the empirical analyses in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same meta-review extraction and augmentation pipeline, coding scheme, o3-mini annotator, and generation and annotation prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ICLR 2021–2024 submissions and reviews, including the rejected-paper evaluation. Review generation, target/aspect annotation, and acceptance-decision tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each experiment, including the three annotation models in Table 2 and eight reviewing models in Table 3. The human-reference comparisons and appendix model sets also match.

E3.justification: Sections 4.2–5 retain the same sampling procedures, annotation sample sizes, default model parameters, review-generation procedures, and agreement and rejection-rate metrics. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The review-distribution analyses in Figures 3–4, annotation confusion matrices in Figures 13–14, and discrepancy case studies in Figures 15–16 are identical. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or revised. The annotation-reliability statistics and distribution summaries remain identical.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Tables 2–5 and 7–12 and the result figures. For example, Table 3 reports DeepSeek-R1's overall F1 as 0.373 in both versions.

T1.justification: The task and coding-category definitions are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or derivations that differ between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same pipeline and dataset contributions and claims about unbalanced reviewing perspectives, neglected novelty assessment, and poor acceptance decisions.

C2.justification: The discussion, limitations, and ethical-impact passages are unchanged, including the restricted ICLR/AI scope, category-level evaluation, annotation discrepancies, and unexplored prompt strategies.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, parameter disclosures, data-collection and access information, and appendix prompts are identical. Hyperlink targets also match. The new acknowledgment supplies no implementation or reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Section 7, citations, and reference entries are unchanged. References reflow across pages 9–10, but no cited work or research-positioning argument is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Acknowledgments section crediting LG AI Research support before Limitation on page 9 and updates the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. The research prose and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment shifts the limitations, ethical-impact, and reference text on pages 9–10. All figures and tables, including appendix displays, retain their content, captions, styling, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds acknowledgment of LG AI Research support, providing additional attribution. The methods, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices; the acknowledgment and limited layout reflow do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
